text.p: These are the leading stories in the Botswana press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- University of Botswana's vice chancellor, Thomas Tlou, has refused to confirm that he will be available for another term of office when his contract ends in June. He has been vice chancellor for 12 years.

- The Botswana government has turned down a request by the South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission to hear evidence in Botswana on cross-border raids by the apartheid era South African Defence Force.

- A proposed two-way satellite presentation by Microsoft chief executive Bill Gates to local and South Africa computer companies is falling flat as local companies say they cannot afford to be at the exhibition in Gaborone.
- The Gazette has slammed Monday's budget for granting civil servants an "over-generous" 9.5 percent pay increase.
